title: Prefix policy generator and safe-apply rollback safeguard
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Autogenerate per-prefix TTL and cache-key coalescing proposals from sampled request traces, run offline hit-rate/cost simulations, and provide a safe-apply plan with automated rollback triggers. Goal: reduce token cost by 12-25% on batchy workloads while keeping tail latency and correctness risk within defined SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Policy generator produces candidate TTL/policy sets for >90% of active prefixes in target service within 12 hours of run.
Offline simulator predicts cost savings and hit-rate delta with confidence intervals; candidate accepted only if median cost reduction >= 10% and 95th percentile latency regression < 5%.
Safe-apply orchestrator can run a staged rollout (10%, 50%, 100%) with automatic rollback on defined signals within 15 minutes of anomaly detection.
A developer can review and approve each candidate via Console and see per-prefix rationale (sampled trace examples, hit-rate forecast, sensitivity to TTL changes).
No customer-visible errors introduced in canary hosts for at least two full traffic cycles (24 hours) during trials.
implementation_steps: Instrument per-prefix request/response sampling pipeline and export compact histograms for prefix popularity, sequence length distribution, and KV reuse patterns.
Build a policy generator module that consumes histograms and outputs candidate TTLs, coalescing keys, and fallback variants with estimated hit-rate and variance.
Integrate generator with existing offline simulator; extend simulator to model batching behavior and KV cache warmup cost across rollout stages.
Add a safety policy layer that annotates TTL changes with risk scores and suggests staging percentages and rollback thresholds.
Expose candidate review UI in Console with links to sampled traces, simulator results, and estimated cost impact per-customer and globally.
Implement orchestrator hooks for staged apply: create canary groups, apply config, monitor signals, escalate or rollback automatically based on thresholds.
Add end-to-end tests and a dry-run mode that only logs simulated effects without touching live caches.
safe_apply_playbook: Stage 1 (dry-run): run generator + simulator; post results to Console draft and notify owners (no config change).
Stage 2 (canary 10%): apply changes to canary pool for 4 hours; monitor key signals (hit-rate, per-token cost, 95th latency, error-rate, token-quality regression).
Stage 3 (ramp 50%): if canary stable for 6 hours, ramp to 50% with continued monitoring and extended retention of KV warmup telemetry.
Stage 4 (full): full rollout after 24 hours of stable signals at 50%; final verification and rollout close-out report.

Rollback triggers: hit-rate drop > 8% relative to baseline AND cost increase > 2%; OR 95th latency regression >= 5% (absolute); OR error-rate increase > 0.1% absolute. Meet any single trigger => immediate rollback to previous policy.
Manual override: SRE/PM can abort rollout via Console; abort creates an incident ticket and pins previous policy.
rollback_steps: Orchestrator marks offending rollout as failed and flips routing back to previous config within target 2 minutes.
Invalidate new KV entries created under the candidate policy (if safe) and allow previous cache state to resume; otherwise, issue a cache flush policy for short windows.
Trigger postmortem collection: collect trace windows (30 minutes before to 30 minutes after trigger), simulator inputs, and a snapshot of policy diffs.
Notify stakeholders and open follow-up tickets for root cause and remediation of generator false-positives.
experiments: A/B test comparing generator TTLs vs baseline static TTL for heavy-tailed prefixes over 2 weeks.
Microbenchmarks that evaluate coalescing strategies (suffix trimming, namespace bucketing, embedding-key canonicalization) on hit-rate and false-positive collisions.
Sensitivity sweep: vary TTL by +- 25% and record cost vs freshness trade-offs to calibrate risk thresholds.
